what_it_does: This paper tackles a cost problem in custom AI chips for wearable devices: each new chip design requires new photomasks (the stencils used in chip fabrication), which are extremely expensive. The proposal is a "via-programmable" base chip where the different neural network layers are configured by changing only the metal interconnect layers (vias—the tiny wires that connect different layers), not the underlying transistor logic. This means one base design can support many different AI models just by varying the wiring. The team also introduces specialized techniques to reduce wiring overhead and compress neural networks to fit efficiently into this programmable architecture.
